BACKGROUND. factory/outcome_contract.py::classify_run(run, scene) classifies one replicate of one scene. Its `scene` argument is a dict {id, pacing_window (int or null), terminal (bool), reveal_ids [str], delivered_before [str], ending_requires [str], non_voiceable_says [str], unlearned_terms [{term, requires}], epilogue_candidates [str]} (read tests/fixtures/outcome_contract/README.md, factory/outcome_contract.py and its tests FIRST; do NOT edit them). `delivered_before` is the set of knowledge ids the player already has when the scene starts; classify_run subtracts it from a turn's grounding ids, so a re-grounded old item is not counted as new progress. Nothing builds this `scene` dict from a story package yet, and `delivered_before` is the missing part. Saved evidence: in a run of scene 2C the narrator re-grounded `k_sl_2b_b_r4` (a scene 2B item) on turn 2, which the contract read as new progress; in scene 2A the entry item `k_scene_2a_entry` and in scene 1B the item `k_sl_1a_b_r1` (scene 1A) were re-grounded the same way.

BUILD `factory/contract_scene.py` with one public function `build_contract_scene(package, scene_id: str) -> dict` (standard library plus the existing storygame.story_package models only; story-agnostic: no story, scene or character names in production code; pure; never mutates the package). It reads the loaded StoryPackage (`package.scenes` gives scene order, `package.knowledge_indexes` and `package.knowledge.knowledge` give items with `available_in_scenes`, `package.pacing.scenes` and `package.pacing.ending` give pacing windows and the ending; look at storygame/story_package/models.py and loader.py `_compile_knowledge_indexes`). Rules:
- `id` is scene_id; raise ValueError for an unknown scene id.
- `reveal_ids`: knowledge ids that are candidates in this scene (`scene_to_candidates[scene_id]`) and are NOT in `delivered_before`, sorted.
- `delivered_before`, sorted: every knowledge id that is (a) available in at least one EARLIER scene (by `package.scenes` order) and not available in this scene, or (b) an entry item of this scene (`item.source.kind` is neither 'storylet_realization' nor 'canonical_route_event', so its source key is `entry:<scene>`; see the loader), because the engine delivers it on entry. An item available in both an earlier scene and this scene is NOT delivered_before by rule (a) (it can still be earned here).
- `pacing_window`: the scene's `handoff_after_turns` from `package.pacing.scenes` if present, else None. `terminal`: true only if the package's pacing `ending` names this scene as its ending scene (read StoryEnding in models.py; if no field names a scene, set terminal false and say so in NOTES.txt). Other fields (`ending_requires`, `non_voiceable_says`, `unlearned_terms`, `epilogue_candidates`): `[]` for now, EXCEPT where the package gives them unambiguously; do not guess, record in NOTES.txt what you left empty.
- The returned dict must have exactly the nine keys above and contain only str/int/bool/None/list/dict values (JSON serialisable).

TESTS, WRITE THEM FIRST in tests/test_contract_scene.py (hermetic, no network, no model; load the real package with `load_story_package(default_package_root())` from storygame.story_package.loader and storygame.story_package.default_root; scene ids are read as `scene.scene_id` on `package.scenes`, which are in play order 1A..3C): (1) for the scene whose id ends 2C: `k_sl_2b_b_r4` is in delivered_before and not in reveal_ids; (2) for 2A: `k_scene_2a_entry` is in delivered_before; (3) for 1B: `k_sl_1a_b_r1` is in delivered_before; (4) the first scene has an empty set from rule (a); (5) unknown scene raises ValueError; (6) the result is JSON serialisable and building twice gives equal results; (7) the package is not mutated (compare a model_dump before and after); (8) integration: build the scene for 2C, then take a one-turn run whose grounding_ids are ['k_sl_2b_b_r4'] with outcome 'committed' (copy the turn field shape from the first case in tests/fixtures/outcome_contract/cases.json) and assert classify_run gives that turn knowledge_progress False. If any of (1)-(3) fails because the item is not shaped as assumed, read the package and adapt the RULE minimally, then say what you found in NOTES.txt; the three saved facts above are the requirement.
